newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU SPONSORS SOCCER SHOW IN ANTI-RACISM DRIVE.
newsitem.headline: EU SPONSORS SOCCER SHOW IN ANTI-RACISM DRIVE.

text.p: Three of world soccer's more temperamental ambassadors will lead a European Commission- sponsored anti-racism drive at a special tournament in Spain in October.
The Commission said on Thursday it would help organise the all-star event on October 12 as part of the European Year Against Racism.
Three teams, including some of the world's top players, will meet in a series of 40-minute matches.

The sides will be captained by Argentine Diego Maradona, a confessed former cocaine addict; France's Eric Cantona, who was banned from the game after an infamous kung-fu style attack on a fan while playing for Manchester United; and Liberian George Weah, the 1995 world player of the year who was banned for head-butting an opponent after a game in November 1996.
"The tournament will bring together some of the best football players in the world, united in their determination to show that racism has no place in our societies," the statement said.
The Commission said more details of the tournament would be announced at a news conference in September.
